newsitem.title: UK: Farmer reticence keeps UK grains market tight.
newsitem.headline: Farmer reticence keeps UK grains market tight.

text.p: There are still plenty of potential buyers in the UK grains market, but farmers' continued unwillingness to sell is keeping traded volumes down, traders said.

Also, the start of the seasonal lull will see many operators squaring positions ahead of the holiday break and standing back from the market. Optimism on export prospects is one of the major supporting factors in the market, with traders citing buyers in eastern Europe as the main potential customers.

But not all feel that the optimism is justified. "Italy, Poland and Spain are all exhausted at the moment (as export prospects)," one UK exporter said. And third country prospects were poor. The UK needed a big third country buyer to come in and take a chunk of grain, he said.

He noted that much of the wheat export potential for the UK was for higher quality. "It leaves out a lot of the midlands, the north and Yorkshire," he said. Wheat from those areas would have to go onto the domestic or the feed export market.
Italian demand for UK feed wheat would be limited this year, closing off some of the UK's usual export opportunities.

The shortage of farm sellers remains a bullish factor for the UK. Normally a rise in sterling, like that seen this morning, would have taken one stg off the wheat future and drawn out origin sellers, one trader said.
But farmers have seen up days and down days over recent weeks and they are selling on the ups, he said.
By the midday break the biggest fall in LIFFE wheat futures was for March, 0.70 stg lower at 97.50.
But physical feed wheat and barley were both quoted 2 stg up on the week this morning.
Day-to-day, sterling remains the main factor driving prices. Its moves against continental currencies, especially the French franc, define UK wheat's position against its major competition.
